Final Order : Acquitted BRIEF STATEMENT OF REASONS FOR THE DECISION:
FACTUAL MATRIX - 1.

Briefly stated, the case of the prosecution is that on 13.06.2017 at 11:30 PM under the Karkarimor Flyover Red Light, Delhi, accused Shamim was found driving a truck,
bearing registration number UP-12L-5166, in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety of others and while driving so, accused struck against a Wagon R car, which was driven by a person namely Sukhbir Singh (deceased), as a result of which the said person namely Sukhbir Singh died.

On the basis of the complaint, FIR was registered under Section 279/304Aof the Indian Penal Code,
1860 (hereinafter, "IPC").
INVESTIGATION AND APPEARANCE OF ACCUSED- 2.

After registration of the FIR, the Investigating Officer (hereinafter, "IO") undertook investigation and on culmination of the investigation, the Police Report under Section 173 Cr.P.C., against the accused persons was filed.
3. Vide order dated 02.08.2018, Ld. Predecessor of this Court took cognizance of the offence and issued summons to the accused.

4. Thereafter, on appearance of accused, copy of charge-sheet alongwith documents annexed therewith were supplied to him as FIR No. 167/2017 PS Jagatpuri State Vs. Shamim Page no. 2 of 7 per section 207 Cr.P.C.
5.

On 02.04.2019, on finding a prima facie case against accused Shamim, notice under Section 279/304A IPC was framed against him by Ld. Predecessor of this Court, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

6. It is pertinent to state here that on 07.05.20252, admission denial u/s 294 Cr. P.C. was conducted, wherein accused admitted following documents;
6.1 Copy of FIR No.167/2017, which was Ex.P1. 6.2 Certificate u/s 65B of Indian Evidence Act,
which was Ex.P2. 6.3 DD No. 6A dated 14.06.2017, which was Ex.P3. 6.4 DD No.15A dated State vs Shamim on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152913549/
2 29.06.2017, which was Ex.P4. 6.5 MLC No.6684 dated 14.06.2017, which was Ex.P5. 6.6 Death summary report, which was Ex.P6. 6.7 Verification of PM report, which was Ex.P7. 6.8 Mechanical Inspection Reports, which were Ex.P8 & Ex.P9. 6.9 TIP order dated 22.07.2017, which was Ex.P10.
6.10 PCR Call Form, which was Ex.P11.
6.11
Dead body identification, which were Ex.P12 & Ex.P13.

Accordingly, witnesses at serial no. 3, 4,
6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 19 were dropped as admitted from the list of witnesses.

PROSECUTION'S EVIDENCE;
7.

In order to substantiate its case, the prosecution has examined only one witness i.e. Deepak Singh as PW-1; 7.1 PW-1 Deepak Singh inter-alia deposed that one day, at around 11:30 PM -12:00 midnight, he was going in a white FIR No. 167/2017 PS Jagatpuri State Vs. Shamim Page no. 3 of 7 color swift car, number of which he did not remember and he had borrowed the said car from his neighbor, to get some food from 24X7 Preet Vihar.

He further deposed that one Wagon R car was in-front of his car and when he reached near fly over from Karkardooma towards Parparganj/flyover from Jagatpuri to Patparganj, he took the road below the flyover and one tempo/truck crossed his car from the left side and came in front of his car and the truck driver applied breaks as it was red light, due to which the above-said Wagon R car got hit with the tempo from behind.

He further deposed that he also applied the breaks and the person inside the Wagon R car got stuck and some public persons along with beggars stopped and with their help, the Wagon R car driver was taken out of the car.
He further deposed that he gave water to the person driving Wagon R from his car and he made a PCR call.

He further deposed that he inquired from the said injured person,
regarding his condition, to which he stated that he was fine and PW-1 made the call to wife of the injured from the mobile phone of the injured and informed about the accident and they came within 5-10 minutes.
He further deposed that the injured refused to go to the hospital when requested by police officials.
He further deposed that his statement was not recorded on that day but later his statement was recorded.
He further deposed that he could not tell the number of the truck or the wagon R car and he could not identify by face the driver of the truck though he was one Muslim person wearing a cap.
He further deposed that he saw that the injured in wagon R car looked tired and sleepy.

At that stage witness was shown the photographs on the judicial file, seeing which witness stated them to be the photographs of the car of the uncle and the same were FIR No. 167/2017 PS Jagatpuri State Vs. Shamim Page no. 4 of 7 exhibited as Ex. A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5.

At that stage, witness was shown the photographs on the judicial file seeing which witness stated them to be the photographs of a truck and the same were exhibited as Ex.A6 to A11 and stated that he could not say whether the same were of offending truck or not.
At that stage, Ld. APP for the State sought permission to cross examine the witness as he was not supporting the case of prosecution and has turned hostile.

During cross examination of PW-1 by Ld.
APP for the State, he deposed that " I can not say with surety whether the date of incident is 13.06.2017.
I can not say whether the no. of Wagon R car was DL 2CAF 4138.

I can not say whether State vs Shamim on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152913549/
3 the no. of the truck was UP 12L 5166 or not.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I can not say whether the Dalla of the truck got open by applying breaks of the truck.
At this stage attention of witness drawn towards accused Shamim present in court today and seeing him witness states that I can not identify and has seen him for the first time in the court today.
It is wrong to suggest that I am deliberately not identifying the accused as I have been influenced by the accused person.
It is further wrong to suggest that I am deliberately concealing the correct and complete facts as I have been won over by the accused.
It is wrong to suggest that I had obtained gratification from the accused and for the same reason I am deposing falsely before the court today.
It is wrong to suggest that I am deliberately not deposing the no. of the offending truck or the identification of the offending truck.
It is wrong to suggest that I am deposing falsely."
PW-1 was not cross examined by ld. Counsel for accused despite being given opportunity.
FIR No. 167/2017 PS Jagatpuri State Vs. Shamim Page no. 5 of 7 8.

entities.text: PS Jagatpuri State Vs. Shamim Page no. 5 of 7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Summons and BWs were repeatedly issued to PW Kapil Bansal (cited as an eye witness) but the same were received back unexecuted.

Since presence of PW Kapil Bansal could not be procured,
hence, he was dropped from the list of witnesses.
9. As can be seen, PW1 Deepak Singh has neither identified the accused in the court nor has assigned any criminal role to the accused and has also not deposed anything incriminating against him.
Moreover, neither there is any other eye witness in the present case nor there is any CCTV footage.

In view of the same, the prosecution evidence stands closed, declining the request of Ld.
Additional Public Prosecutor for leading further evidence, as it shall be futile to record the testimonies of other witnesses, who are formal or official in nature.

The precious Court time should not be wasted in recording the evidence of formal or official witnesses when the prosecution witness,
i.e. PW1, has not supported the case of the prosecution.
The statement under section 313 of the Cr.P.C of accused is dispensed with as there is nothing incriminating against him.
10. I have heard the arguments of Ld. APP for State and Mr. R.H. Zaidi, Ld. defence counsel.
I have also perused the case file carefully.
11. It has been held in case of Sadhu Singh V/s State of Punjab 1997(3) Crime 55 the Hon'ble Punjab & Haryana High Court :-

entities.text: Sadhu Singh V/s State of Punjab 1997(3) Crime 55
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "In a criminal trial, it is for the prosecution to establish its case beyond all reasonable doubts.
It is for the prosecution to travel the entire distance from may have to must have.

If the prosecution appears to be improbable or lacks credibility the benefit of doubt necessarily has to go to the accused."
FIR No. 167/2017 PS Jagatpuri State Vs. Shamim Page no. 6 of 7 DECISION 12.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, with the prosecution failing to prove its case against the accused person beyond reasonable doubt, accused Shamim S/o Yusuf, stands acquitted for the State vs Shamim on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152913549/
4 offence u/s 279/304A IPC in FIR no.167/2017, PS Jafrabad.
13.
Case property, if any, shall be disposed of as per rules, after expiration of period of appeal and as per law.
Case file be consigned to the record room after due compliance.
Digitally signed by AAYUSHI ANNOUNCED IN OPEN COURT TODAY i.e. 07.05.2025.
